newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SLOVENIAN PM TAKES "FIRM" STANCE ON RAIL STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVENIAN PM TAKES "FIRM" STANCE ON RAIL STRIKE.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Tuesday his government would adopt a firm stance with striking railway workers who have crippled cargo traffic in the west of the country.

"The railway strike started today and the government has a firm position," Drnovsek said in Hungary, where he held talks with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn on trilateral issues.
"There is not much room for manoeuvre to compromise (and we) don't want it to spread to another sector," he said in a response to a question at a joint news conference.
"So the government is relatively firm," he added.
Slovenian railway workers started a 10-day strike to press for higher salaries and holiday pay, leaving cargo transport crippled in the west of the country but passenger transport unaffected.
The rail strike is the fifth to hit the tiny Alpine nation this year after two one-hour and two four-hour warning strikes by railway workers earlier.
